info.title: HireD API
info.description:
HireD Phase 1 backend REST API. Built from the PRD v0.2 (30 Sep 2026), the database design v1.2 and the Technical Guidelines (section 7).

**Base path:** `/api/v1`. **Routes:** kebab-case. **JSON keys:** snake_case, same as the database columns.

**Success response:** `{ "success": true, "data": ..., "message": "..." }`.
**Error response:** `{ "success": false, "error": { "code": "...", "message": "...", "details": [...] } }`.

**Status codes:** 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 malformed request, 401 not logged in, 403 not allowed, 404 not found (also used when a partner or driver asks for another user's row), 409 conflict with the current state (wrong status, version changed, duplicate), 422 validation failed, 500 server error.

**Lists** use `page` (default 1) and `limit` (default 20, max 100) and return `data: { items, page, limit, total }`. The guidelines do not define pagination, so this is a team choice.

**Login:** the access token (JWT) lives 15 minutes and the refresh token 7 days. Send `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`. On 401, call `/auth/refresh` once, then retry. If refresh fails, log in again. 5 wrong logins lock the account for 15 minutes.

**Own data only:** `company_id` and `driver_id` come from the token, never from the request. A partner or driver never sends their own id.

**Money and percentages** are decimal strings such as `"10000.00"` and `"30.00"` (NUMERIC in PostgreSQL, no floating point). **Times** are ISO 8601 in UTC. **Months** (`YYYY-MM`) and report days follow Asia/Kolkata time.

**Concurrent edits:** orders, trips and invoices carry a `version`. Send the version you read. If another admin changed the row first you get 409 `VERSION_CONFLICT`: reload and retry.

**Files:** uploads are `multipart/form-data`, only image/jpeg, image/png and application/pdf, max 5 MB. Storage paths are never returned. To open a private file, ask for its `.../link` endpoint and use the signed URL within 5 minutes.

**Every operation has `x-prd`:** the PRD requirement IDs it covers.

**Not an endpoint:** the trip-close payout, the wallet credit and the audit log are written by the backend inside the trip-close transaction. There is no endpoint to create a payroll row or a wallet credit.

**Open points (not decided in the PRD, so not built):**
1. How a new driver gets an account. The PRD has an onboarding queue (A-09) and document upload (D-02), but the database says only ACTIVE drivers can log in. No driver sign-up or admin-creates-driver endpoint exists yet.
2. Whether expenses are paid back to the driver (PRD 8.3). Today they are display-only.
3. Push/SMS alerts. Only emails exist (B-07).
4. Exact meaning of "on time" (15 minutes after pickup) and "success rate" (CLOSED trips / ACCEPTED orders) in the reports.

patch.summary: Activate or deactivate an admin account
patch.description:
**Access:** ADMIN.

ACTIVE <-> INACTIVE switches access. Deactivation revokes all active sessions for that admin transactionally. Prevents self-deactivation. Enforces maintaining at least two active admins for two-person verification. Audited as USER_DEACTIVATED or USER_REACTIVATED.

**Access:** ADMIN.

One endpoint, two steps. **Step 1:** the admin who created a DRAFT invoice approves it, so verified_by_admin_id1 = creator and status becomes PENDING_VERIFICATION. **Step 2:** a different admin approves a PENDING_VERIFICATION invoice, so verified_by_admin_id2 is set and status becomes VERIFIED. The creator cannot give the second approval. Both approvals record who and when. Audited as INVOICE_APPROVED.

Converts the order into a trip (status UNASSIGNED). The admin confirms or sets the total trip amount here. The backend creates the 6-digit OTP and calculates the ETA with the maps service (admin may override with `eta`). The partner gets an ORDER_ACCEPTED email (PRD B-07). post.summary: Close the trip with the OTP
post.description:
**Access:** DRIVER.

Allowed only after expenses are confirmed. The driver types the 6-digit code the partner gave. All steps run in one transaction: lock the trip, check the code, set CLOSED, write the payroll row (rate frozen), credit the wallet, write the audit rows. A wrong code adds 1 to otp_attempts and the trip stays open. At 5 wrong codes the trip is locked until an admin resets it. Sending the request twice pays the driver only once.

403.description: Too many wrong codes. An admin must reset the OTP.

error.message: Too many wrong codes. An admin must reset the OTP.

409.description: Trip is not ONGOING, or expenses are not confirmed.

error.message: Trip is not ONGOING, or expenses are not confirmed.

422.description: Wrong code. The trip stays open.

error.message: Wrong code. The trip stays open.

post.description:

Sets expenses_confirmed = true, even when the list is empty. Required before the trip can be closed (PRD D-09).

otp.description: The 6-digit code the partner gives the driver. Send as text to keep leading zeros.

wallet_credit.description: Driver share credited to the wallet.

CloseTripResult.description: Trip close runs as one database transaction: trip CLOSED, payroll row, wallet credit, audit rows. The driver is paid exactly once.

TripReportPartner.description: PRD B-05. Visible only after the trip is CLOSED. Does not show the split or shares.

unbilled_payrolls.description: Payroll rows with no invoice for a past month.

unpaid_payrolls.description: Payroll rows where payment_status is UNPAID.

mismatched_invoices.description: Invoices whose totals differ from the sum of their payroll rows.

DriverDelayRow.description: Delay = started_at - pickup_time when above zero.

on_time_rate.description: Trips started within 15 min of pickup_time / trips with started_at, in %.

trip_status.description: Outcome of the order, empty if rejected or not yet a trip.
